title: Time-Dependent Hamiltonian Simulation with Optimal Query Complexity
authors: Boyang Chen, Minbo Gao, Xinzhao Wang, Shuo Zhou
abstract: We give a query-optimal algorithm for simulating a general $n$-qubit time-dependent Hamiltonian $H(t)$ on $[0,T]$, assuming that $H$ is Lipschitz continuous and $\|H(t)\|\leqα$. In the standard $\mathrm{HAM\mbox{-}T}$ access model, the algorithm approximates the time-ordered propagator $U_H(T)$ to error $\varepsilon$ using $$ O\left(   αT+\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)}   {\log(e+\log(1/\varepsilon)/(αT))}   \right) $$ $\mathrm{HAM\mbox{-}T}$ queries. This matches the known query lower bound for time-independent Hamiltonians, showing that time dependence incurs no asymptotic query overhead.   Our method first constructs a one-query transducer that, given an auxiliary state, implements an approximation to $U_H(T)$ and returns the state unchanged. A weighted combination of circuits that apply the transducer different numbers of times makes the error caused by omitting this state decay factorially, yielding the stated optimal precision dependence. For time-independent Hamiltonians, the same method also gives a query-optimal alternative to qubitization.
summary: This paper presents a query-optimal algorithm for simulating general time-dependent quantum Hamiltonians using the HAM-T model. By utilizing advanced transducer techniques and error analysis involving weighted circuit combinations, they achieve a complexity that matches theoretical lower bounds. This is significant because it proves that modeling time dependence does not incur an asymptotic overhead in terms of required queries.
main_problem: Determining the optimal query complexity for simulating a general time-dependent Hamiltonian $H(t)$ over a finite time interval $[0, T]$.
main_result: The authors achieve an algorithm with query complexity matching the known lower bound, demonstrating that general time dependence does not introduce asymptotic overhead compared to time-independent cases.
method: They employ a novel one-query transducer framework combined with a weighted combination of reuse circuits to ensure factorial decay in simulation error.
model_or_system: The system is governed by quantum dynamics dictated by $H(t)$, and the target operation is the time-ordered propagator $U_H(T)$. The analysis is conducted within the time-indexed block-encoding-access model (HAM-T).
key_observables: Query complexity, simulation error ($\epsilon$), and the evolution time scale ($\alpha T$).
important_parameters: Lipschitz constant ($ eta$) of $H(t)$, total time $T$, and desired precision $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The Hamiltonian $H(t)$ is assumed to be Lipschitz continuous, and the analysis operates in the worst-case black-box query complexity setting.

paper_structure: The work progresses by first establishing the optimal query complexity using a transducer framework, then refining the error analysis through weighted combinations of reuse circuits to achieve factorial precision decay. Later sections explore continuous-time analogues and subspace constructions for theoretical completeness.
why_interesting: This work provides state-of-the-art results on quantum simulation complexity, directly impacting how efficiently we can model time evolution in complex physical systems using limited query access models.
